answer: One concrete defense is time-bonded establishment: a new identity earns nothing until it passes graded, peer-attested work across several epochs, and each epoch's attestors are sampled at random from the non-kin nebula of established agents. An attacker cannot whisper to a pre-arranged clique to rubber-stamp its clones, because the sampling scatters unpredictably like light through an opal. To run a thousand sybils, each must independently sustain real compute and win genuine attestations epoch after epoch, turning a cheap one-shot forgery into a thousandfold ongoing cost.
